The search turned up mostly 2022 coverage of *Gemini Rights*, Steve Lacy's second album, released July 15, 2022 on RCA.

**Production:** Lacy handled most of the work himself. Per one Grammy.com piece, the record is majorly self-produced by Lacy, and it has only one guest appearance. In an Apple Music interview with Zane Lowe, he put his share at roughly 90%, saying he had tried to bring in an executive producer but ended up still doing it. Another source notes that he made the album with the full studio treatment, after his earlier records were made on an iPhone and a laptop.

**Interview themes:** In the Grammy.com interview, Lacy described the album as essentially me coming into myself after a breakup. The same piece covers how exploring his own red flags helped him trust his instincts, and why directing a video with his mother and siblings was "too much" for him.

**Sound and content:** Reviewers describe the lead single "Mercury" as bossa nova-influenced and say it samples soul singer Eddie Kendrick's "Just Memories". A later retrospective notes the album takes a more serious approach to love and relationships than his debut, *Apollo XXI*.

**Length and philosophy:** The album runs 10 tracks and about 35 minutes. Lacy explained the brevity by saying he wanted listeners to make a decision to want to keep playing it again.

**Guests:** Fousheé appears on "Sunshine," and Matt Martians, his bandmate in The Internet, appears on "2gether."

The results don't cover anything after 2022, so later reflections on the album aren't included.
